# Laravel Loom

> Static analyzer for Laravel's event-driven primitives — emits a deterministic JSON index.

# Laravel Loom

## Understand it

- [What Loom sees](concepts/what-loom-sees.md): what a scan records and what it can't resolve.
- [The index](concepts/the-index.md): how to read one flow forward and backward.

## Use it

- [Browse the UI](guides/browse-the-ui.md): the read-only `/loom` dashboard and chain graph.
- [Ask an agent](guides/ask-an-agent.md): serve the index to an agent through the MCP server.
- [Use with Laravel Boost](guides/use-with-boost.md): register the MCP server next to Boost's.
- [Gate your CI](guides/gate-your-ci.md): diff and check the index on every pull request.
- [Why was my code missed?](guides/why-was-my-code-missed.md): trace a missing entry to its cause.

# Getting started

Scan a Laravel 12.41+ or 13 app on PHP 8.3+, follow one event, and see the same data in the browser.

```bash
composer require lucasp1337/laravel-loom --dev
php artisan loom:scan
```

```text
Loom index written to /var/www/shop/storage/loom/index.json
Scanned 11 PHP files in 1 directories.
events: 4, listeners: 4, observers: 0, model events: 0, jobs: 1, unresolved dispatches: 1, closure listeners: 1, scheduled tasks: 0, mailables: 0, notifications: 0, routes: 2, unresolved routes: 0, skipped files: 0
```

The scan reads your source and never boots your app. The last line counts each section of the index it wrote.

## Follow an event

Print the index filtered to one event:

```bash
php artisan loom:show OrderPlaced
```

```json
{
    "id": "App\\Events\\OrderPlaced",
    "fqcn": "App\\Events\\OrderPlaced",
    "kind": "class",
    "file": "app/Events/OrderPlaced.php",
    "line": 5,
    "dispatched_from": [
        {
            "file": "app/Http/Controllers/OrderController.php",
            "line": 11,
            "method": "App\\Http\\Controllers\\OrderController::store"
        }
    ],
    "handled_by": [
        {
            "listener": "App\\Listeners\\SendReceipt",
            "method": "handle"
        }
    ]
}
```

`dispatched_from` lists where your code fires the event and `handled_by` every listener that reacts. You never registered `SendReceipt`: Loom linked it through the type hint on `handle()`. The filter applies to events, listeners, observers and model events; other sections print in full ([`loom:show`](reference/commands.md#loomshow)). [The index](concepts/the-index.md) shows how to follow the chain from here.

## Open the UI

With `livewire/livewire` installed, Loom mounts a read-only UI at `/loom` in the `local` environment. It reads the index and never scans. [Browse the UI](guides/browse-the-ui.md) covers the chain graph and opening it elsewhere.

## When it doesn't work

### No index yet

Without a scan, `loom:show` fails:

```text
Loom index not found at /var/www/shop/storage/loom/index.json. Run `php artisan loom:scan` first.
```

### A dispatch is missing

A call like `event($class)` lands in `unresolved_dispatches`, with a file and line, because the class isn't named in the source. [Why was my code missed?](guides/why-was-my-code-missed.md) covers the rest.

## Where to next

- [Gate your CI](guides/gate-your-ci.md) on the index.
- [Ask an agent](guides/ask-an-agent.md) through the MCP server.
- [Recipes](recipes/event-chain.md) for common questions.

# What Loom sees

Loom reads your source without booting the app and records what it finds, one index section per primitive.

```text
Loom index written to /var/www/shop/storage/loom/index.json
Scanned 11 PHP files in 1 directories.
events: 4, listeners: 4, observers: 0, model events: 0, jobs: 1, unresolved dispatches: 1, closure listeners: 1, scheduled tasks: 0, mailables: 0, notifications: 0, routes: 2, unresolved routes: 0, skipped files: 0
```

The sections and their fields are in the [schema](../reference/schema.md#top-level-fields). The code shapes each scanner reads, and the ones it skips, are tested examples under [What Loom detects](../reference/detection/index.md).

## Why a static index

One event is wired in several files: dispatched in a controller, handled by a listener linked only by the type hint on `handle()`, and by a closure a provider registers. Grep finds the dispatch and the closure, not the listener. Loom follows each link and stores it in [one index](the-index.md), so it reports what your code says, not what one request did.

## What Loom can't see

A class picked at runtime has no name in the source. Loom lists each such call in `unresolved_dispatches` or `unresolved_routes` with its file, line and a `reason` instead of dropping it. The [reason table](../reference/detection/index.md#unresolved-reasons) leads from a `reason` to the code that produces it, and `loom:check` can [fail on new ones](../recipes/new-unresolved-dispatches.md).

If something you expected is missing, start at [Why was my code missed?](../guides/why-was-my-code-missed.md)

# The index

A scan writes one JSON document, `storage/loom/index.json`: metadata, `stats`, then one array per primitive.

```json
{
  "schema_version": "1.0",
  "loom_version": "0.4.0",
  "scanned_at": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "laravel_version": "13.0",
  "stats": {"events":4,"model_events":0,"listeners":4,"observers":0,"jobs":1,"unresolved_dispatches":1,"closure_listeners":1,"scheduled_tasks":0,"routes":2,"unresolved_routes":0,"mailables":0,"notifications":0},
  "events": [ { "...": "..." } ],
  "model_events": [ { "...": "..." } ],
  "listeners": [ { "...": "..." } ],
  "observers": [ { "...": "..." } ],
  "jobs": [ { "...": "..." } ],
  "unresolved_dispatches": [ { "...": "..." } ],
  "closure_listeners": [ { "...": "..." } ],
  "scheduled_tasks": [ { "...": "..." } ],
  "routes": [ { "...": "..." } ],
  "unresolved_routes": [ { "...": "..." } ],
  "mailables": [ { "...": "..." } ],
  "notifications": [ { "...": "..." } ]
}
```

Every key is always present and `stats` counts each section. Entries are sorted, so two scans of the same source differ only in `scanned_at`, which keeps [`loom:diff`](../guides/gate-your-ci.md#see-what-changed) output stable. The [schema](../reference/schema.md) has the field-by-field contract.

## Reading a relationship

Every relationship is stored once, on whichever side owns it:

| Field | Lives on | Each item |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dispatches` | route, listener, job, observer, closure listener | `{target, kind, confidence, file, line}` |
| `handled_by` | event | `{listener, method}` |
| `dispatched_from` | event, job | `{file, line, method}` |
| `sent_from` | mailable | `{file, line, method}` |
| `notified_from` | notification | `{file, line, method}` |

Read an event's `handled_by` for its handlers and a job's `dispatched_from` for its callers. `kind` says what a target is, and [`confidence`](../reference/schema.md#dispatchconfidence) how it was resolved.

## A worked example

`POST /orders` runs `OrderController::store`, which dispatches `OrderPlaced`. `SendReceipt` handles it and dispatches a queued `SendMail` job.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    R[POST /orders] -->|dispatches| E(OrderPlaced event)
    E -->|handled_by| L[SendReceipt]
    L -->|dispatches| J(SendMail job)
```

These entries come from a scan of that flow, trimmed to the fields that carry the links. The route:

```json
{
    "method": "POST",
    "uri": "/orders",
    "name": "orders.store",
    "controller_fqcn": "App\\Http\\Controllers\\OrderController",
    "controller_method": "store",
    "file": "routes/web.php",
    "line": 6,
    "dispatches": [
        {
            "target": "App\\Events\\OrderPlaced",
            "kind": "event",
            "confidence": "high",
            "file": "app/Http/Controllers/OrderController.php",
            "line": 11
        }
    ]
}
```

The event:

```json
{
    "id": "App\\Events\\OrderPlaced",
    "file": "app/Events/OrderPlaced.php",
    "line": 5,
    "dispatched_from": [
        {
            "file": "app/Http/Controllers/OrderController.php",
            "line": 11,
            "method": "App\\Http\\Controllers\\OrderController::store"
        }
    ],
    "handled_by": [
        {
            "listener": "App\\Listeners\\SendReceipt",
            "method": "handle"
        }
    ]
}
```

The listener:

```json
{
    "fqcn": "App\\Listeners\\SendReceipt",
    "file": "app/Listeners/SendReceipt.php",
    "line": 9,
    "handles": [
        {
            "event": "App\\Events\\OrderPlaced",
            "method": "handle"
        }
    ],
    "registration": "discovery_unverified",
    "queued": false,
    "dispatches": [
        {
            "target": "App\\Events\\ReceiptSent",
            "kind": "event",
            "confidence": "high",
            "file": "app/Listeners/SendReceipt.php",
            "line": 13
        },
        {
            "target": "App\\Jobs\\SendMail",
            "kind": "job",
            "confidence": "high",
            "file": "app/Listeners/SendReceipt.php",
            "line": 14
        }
    ]
}
```

The job:

```json
{
    "fqcn": "App\\Jobs\\SendMail",
    "file": "app/Jobs/SendMail.php",
    "line": 7,
    "queued": true,
    "dispatched_from": [
        {
            "file": "app/Listeners/SendReceipt.php",
            "line": 14,
            "method": "App\\Listeners\\SendReceipt::handle"
        }
    ]
}
```

The route's `dispatches` names `OrderPlaced`, whose `handled_by` names `SendReceipt`, whose `dispatches` names `SendMail`. Read backward, `SendMail.dispatched_from` points at `SendReceipt::handle`. A closure registered for `OrderPlaced` is not in `handled_by`: it has its own `closure_listeners` entry.

Commit the index if you want a baseline to [diff and check](../guides/gate-your-ci.md) a branch against; otherwise add it to `.gitignore`. The [PHP API](../reference/php-api.md) reads it as typed objects.

# Browse the UI

Open `/loom` in your local app and follow `OrderPlaced` through every listener and job it triggers.

```bash
composer require livewire/livewire --dev
php artisan loom:scan
php artisan serve
```

Open `http://localhost:8000/loom`. The dashboard counts each primitive, lists orphans (events nobody handles, listeners with no event, unresolved dispatches) and ranks events by fan-out. The UI reads the index and never scans, so scan again after you change code.

## Follow an event

Click **Events**, then `OrderPlaced`. The page lists where the event is dispatched, the listeners that handle it and what they dispatch next. Click **View chain** to see the trail as a graph, one column per hop:

- Click a node to read its facts and open its page.
- Double-click a node to collapse or expand it.
- The depth selector sets how many hops are drawn. Depth and selection live in the address bar, so the link reopens the same view.

Jobs, mailables and notifications are leaves, and observers are not drawn. Which calls count as a listener's dispatches is shown in [Dispatches](../reference/detection/dispatches.md).

| Message | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `Depth limit reached. Raise the depth to expand the remaining events.` | Handlers exist past the edge; pick a higher depth. |
| `No handlers registered for this event.` | Nothing in the index handles it; see [Why was my code missed?](why-was-my-code-missed.md) |
| `↺ already shown` | The event was drawn on another branch. It isn't always a loop: the `cyclic-dispatch` rule of [`loom:check`](../reference/check-rules-and-formats.md#rules) reports real cycles. |

## Find things

Each sidebar section is a table you can filter and sort; the address bar keeps the view, so `/loom/listeners?q=Order&sort=dispatch_count&dir=desc` is a saved search. Press `Ctrl K` (`Cmd K`) or `/` to search every section by class, route or file.

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `Ctrl K` / `Cmd K`, or `/` | Open the palette |
| Esc | Close the palette or drawer; deselect a node |
| `g` then `d` | Dashboard |
| `g` then `e` | Events |
| `g` then `l` | Listeners |
| `g` then `o` | Observers |
| `g` then `j` | Jobs |
| `g` then `c` | Closure listeners |
| `g` then `m` | Mailables |
| `g` then `n` | Notifications |
| `g` then `r` | Routes |

## When the page isn't what you expect

| You see | Do |
| --- | --- |
| 503 `No index found` or `Index could not be loaded` | Run `php artisan loom:scan` |
| 403 | The `viewLoom` gate refused you; see below |
| 404 on `/loom` | Add the environment to `ui.environments`, check `ui.enabled`, and run `php artisan route:clear` if routes are cached |
| `Index is 6 days older than your last commit to app/` | Run `php artisan loom:scan`. The banner compares commits, so it never shows for uncommitted changes or outside a git checkout. |

## Open it on staging

List the environment in `ui.environments`, then define the `viewLoom` gate; yours replaces the default, which allows only `local`:

```php
Gate::define('viewLoom', fn (?User $user): bool => in_array($user?->email, ['dev@shop.test'], true));
```

The gate runs on every page load and every click. `production` is ignored unless `ui.allow_in_production` is `true`. The path, domain and kill switch are in [UI configuration](../reference/ui-config.md#browser-ui).

# Ask an agent about your events

Register `loom:mcp` with your MCP client so an agent answers from the index instead of grepping your source.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "loom": {
      "command": "php",
      "args": ["/var/www/shop/artisan", "loom:mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

Put that in your client's MCP config, such as `.mcp.json` at the project root, and restart the client. The server needs `laravel/mcp` (`composer require laravel/mcp --dev`). Use an absolute path to `artisan`; under Docker or Sail, run `php artisan loom:mcp` inside the container without a TTY.

## Ask a question

Ask "What happens when an order is placed?". The agent calls `events-following` for `OrderPlaced` and gets the handlers, what they dispatch and the handlers of those, each with a file and line:

```json
{
    "root": "App\\Events\\OrderPlaced",
    "depth": 3,
    "edges": [
        {
            "event": "App\\Events\\OrderPlaced",
            "handler": "App\\Listeners\\SendReceipt::handle",
            "handler_kind": "listener",
            "dispatches": [
                {
                    "target": "App\\Events\\ReceiptSent",
                    "kind": "event",
                    "confidence": "high",
                    "file": "app/Listeners/SendReceipt.php",
                    "line": 13
                },
                {
                    "target": "App\\Jobs\\SendMail",
                    "kind": "job",
                    "confidence": "high",
                    "file": "app/Listeners/SendReceipt.php",
                    "line": 14
                }
            ]
        },
        {
            "event": "App\\Events\\ReceiptSent",
            "handler": "App\\Listeners\\ArchiveReceipt::handle",
            "handler_kind": "listener",
            "dispatches": []
        },
        {
            "event": "App\\Events\\ReceiptSent",
            "handler": "app/Providers/EventServiceProvider.php:14",
            "handler_kind": "closure",
            "dispatches": [
                {
                    "target": "App\\Events\\ReceiptLogged",
                    "kind": "event",
                    "confidence": "high",
                    "file": "app/Providers/EventServiceProvider.php",
                    "line": 15
                }
            ]
        },
        {
            "event": "App\\Events\\ReceiptLogged",
            "handler": "App\\Listeners\\WriteAuditLog::handle",
            "handler_kind": "listener",
            "dispatches": []
        }
    ],
    "events_reached": [
        "App\\Events\\OrderPlaced",
        "App\\Events\\ReceiptSent",
        "App\\Events\\ReceiptLogged"
    ],
    "cycles": [],
    "truncated": false
}
```

The [MCP tools](../reference/mcp-tools.md#which-tool-answers-what) page lists which tool answers which question, with inputs and real responses. Name classes in full (`App\Events\OrderPlaced`): tools match fully qualified names exactly.

## Where the index comes from

The server reads the index `loom:scan` wrote, at `index_path`, and reloads it when the file changes. With no flag it scans once, on the first tool call, if the file is missing. On a shared machine or in CI, make a missing index an error:

```bash
php artisan loom:mcp --no-scan
```

```text
ERROR  No index at [storage/loom/index.json] and --no-scan is set. Run `php artisan loom:scan` first.
```

`--scan` scans before serving, `--no-scan` never scans, `--allow-empty` lets a scan with no PHP files write an empty index and `--snapshot=PATH` serves another file; see [Commands](../reference/commands.md#loommcp). The server answers from your last scan, not your working tree, so rescan after you change code.

!!! warning "Keep stdout clean"
    Client and server talk JSON-RPC over stdout. A stray `echo`, a `dd()` or a PHP notice breaks the connection: log to a file and set `display_errors=stderr` for the CLI.

## What the agent can't see

A dispatch like `event($this->followUp)` names no class, so it is never a `target`. `find-unresolved-dispatches` lists these:

```json
{
    "count": 1,
    "unresolved_dispatches": [
        {
            "file": "app/Jobs/SendMail.php",
            "line": 13,
            "expression": "event($this->followUp)",
            "reason": "stored_target"
        }
    ]
}
```

Check this list before you trust "nothing listens to X". Each dispatch carries a [`confidence`](../reference/schema.md#dispatchconfidence); chain responses report `truncated` when `depth` cut them short.

# Use Loom with Laravel Boost

Teach agents in a [Laravel Boost](https://laravel.com/docs/boost) project when to call Loom, and register its server next to Boost's.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "laravel-boost": {
      "command": "php",
      "args": ["artisan", "boost:mcp"]
    },
    "loom": {
      "command": "php",
      "args": ["artisan", "loom:mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

Boost registers only its own server, so add the `loom` entry to your MCP config yourself and restart the agent. The server needs `laravel/mcp`; [Ask an agent](ask-an-agent.md) covers Docker, paths and what to ask.

## What Boost picks up

Loom ships two files under `resources/boost/`, which Boost reads from each direct Composer dependency:

| File | Boost loads it as | It says |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `resources/boost/guidelines/core.blade.php` | A guideline, every session | When to call Loom, which tool answers what, and not to guess unresolved dispatches |
| `resources/boost/skills/loom/SKILL.md` | A skill, on demand | Workflows for impact analysis, orphans and tracing a route to its events |

Run `php artisan boost:install` (or `boost:update`) and select Loom when Boost lists third-party packages. The guideline tells agents to run `php artisan loom:scan` after changing events, listeners, jobs or routes.

# Gate your CI on architecture

Fail pull requests that add a dead event, a dispatch loop or an unresolved dispatch, and show reviewers what changed.

```bash
php artisan loom:scan
php artisan loom:check
```

```text
orphan-listeners — Every listener handles at least one event
  ✗ Listener App\Listeners\AuditOrders handles no events.
orphan-events — Every event is dispatched or handled
  ✗ Event App\Events\OrderCancelled is never dispatched and never handled.
cyclic-dispatch — No cyclic event/job dispatch chains
  ✗ Cyclic dispatch: App\Events\InventoryAdjusted → App\Events\OrderPlaced → App\Events\InventoryAdjusted
3 violation(s) across 3 rule(s).
```

The branch added a listener pair that dispatch each other's events; the app also has an unused event and an untyped listener. `loom:check` exits `1` on a violation and `2` when it couldn't run, so fail the job on any non-zero code. Each rule and its fix is in [Check rules](../reference/check-rules-and-formats.md#rules).

Without a reference point `unresolved-dispatches` checks nothing. Compare against a baseline to [fail on new unresolved dispatches](../recipes/new-unresolved-dispatches.md), or pass `--strict` to fail on all of them.

## See what changed

`loom:diff` lists what moved between two indexes:

```bash
php artisan loom:diff .loom/baseline.json storage/loom/index.json
```

```text
events
  + {"id":"App\\Events\\InventoryAdjusted","fqcn":"App\\Events\\InventoryAdjusted","kind":"class","file":"app/Events/InventoryAdjusted.php","line":5,"dispatched_from":[{"file":"app/Listeners/ReserveStock.php","line":12,"method":"App\\Listeners\\ReserveStock::handle"}],"handled_by":[{"listener":"App\\Listeners\\RecountStock","method":"handle"}]}
  ~ App\Events\OrderPlaced
      handled_by:
        + {"listener":"App\\Listeners\\ReserveStock","method":"handle"}
      dispatched_from:
        + {"file":"app/Listeners/RecountStock.php","line":12,"method":"App\\Listeners\\RecountStock::handle"}

listeners
  + {"fqcn":"App\\Listeners\\RecountStock","file":"app/Listeners/RecountStock.php","line":8,"handles":[{"event":"App\\Events\\InventoryAdjusted","method":"handle"}],"registration":"discovery_unverified","queued":false,"dispatches":[{"target":"App\\Events\\OrderPlaced","kind":"event","confidence":"high","file":"app/Listeners/RecountStock.php","line":12}]}
  + {"fqcn":"App\\Listeners\\ReserveStock","file":"app/Listeners/ReserveStock.php","line":8,"handles":[{"event":"App\\Events\\OrderPlaced","method":"handle"}],"registration":"discovery_unverified","queued":false,"dispatches":[{"target":"App\\Events\\InventoryAdjusted","kind":"event","confidence":"high","file":"app/Listeners/ReserveStock.php","line":12}]}

unresolved_dispatches
  + {"file":"app/Services/Notifier.php","line":9,"expression":"event($eventClass)","reason":"dynamic_class_name"}
```

`+` is an added entry and `~` one whose links changed. Like `git diff --exit-code`, it exits `1` when anything changed and `2` on bad input, so a bare `loom:diff` step fails the job; fail only on `2`.

## Run both on every pull request

The Loom Action scans the branch, runs `loom:check`, diffs against the base branch and posts one sticky PR comment:

```yaml
name: Loom
on: pull_request

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write

jobs:
  loom:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: lucasp1337/laravel-loom@v0.4.0
        with:
          strict: "true"
```

The job fails with the exit code of `loom:check`. The Action never passes a baseline, so set `strict: "true"` or unresolved dispatches go unchecked. If the base branch can't be scanned, the diff is skipped and the job still passes. Inputs, outputs and the fork limit are in the [Action reference](../reference/action.md).

# Why was my code missed?

When an entry is missing or a link is empty, first look for its file in the unresolved lists.

```bash
php artisan loom:scan
jq '.unresolved_dispatches[], .unresolved_routes[] | select(.file == "app/Http/Controllers/OrderController.php")' storage/loom/index.json
```

**1. Read the reason.** Loom lists a call it recognised but could not resolve, with its file, line and `reason`. Find the reason in the [reason table](../reference/detection/index.md#unresolved-reasons); it links to the example that produces it, next to the form Loom does read.

**2. Find your code shape on the primitive's page.** Some forms leave no trace. Compare your code with the examples for [listeners](../reference/detection/listeners.md), [jobs](../reference/detection/jobs.md), [routes](../reference/detection/routes.md) and the rest under [What Loom detects](../reference/detection/index.md). A line marked `✗ not recorded` is a form Loom skips.

**3. Check that the file was scanned.** `php artisan loom:scan -v` lists files skipped for syntax errors. Code outside [`scan.paths`](../reference/scan-config.md), or under `scan.exclude`, is never read.

If your code matches a form the docs say is read and still doesn't show up, [open an issue](https://github.com/lucasp1337/laravel-loom/issues) with the snippet.

# What runs when an event fires

Follow `handled_by` and `dispatches` from one event down to the last handler.

```php
use Lucasp\Loom\Index\IndexLoader;

$index = (new IndexLoader)->fromFile('storage/loom/index.json');

$follow = function (string $event, string $indent = '', array $path = []) use (&$follow, $index): void {
    if (in_array($event, $path, true)) {
        echo "{$indent}(cycle)\n";

        return;
    }

    // Listener classes, then closures registered for the event.
    $handlers = collect($index->handlersOf($event))
        ->mapWithKeys(fn ($handler) => [
            "{$handler->listener}::{$handler->method}" => $index->findListener($handler->listener)?->dispatches ?? [],
        ])
        ->merge(collect($index->closureListeners())->where('event', $event)->mapWithKeys(fn ($closure) => [
            "closure at {$closure->file}:{$closure->line}" => $closure->dispatches,
        ]));

    foreach ($handlers as $handler => $dispatches) {
        echo "{$indent}{$handler}\n";
        foreach ($dispatches as $dispatch) {
            echo "{$indent}  → {$dispatch->kind->value} {$dispatch->target}\n";
            $follow($dispatch->target, "{$indent}    ", [...$path, $event]);
        }
    }
};

$follow('App\Events\OrderPlaced');
```

```text title="Output"
App\Listeners\SendReceipt::handle
  → event App\Events\ReceiptSent
    App\Listeners\ArchiveReceipt::handle
    closure at app/Providers/EventServiceProvider.php:14
      → event App\Events\ReceiptLogged
        App\Listeners\WriteAuditLog::handle
  → job App\Jobs\SendMail
```

A listener's `dispatches` covers its whole class. The `events-following` [MCP tool](../reference/mcp-tools.md) returns the same chain as JSON, with a depth limit. Loading the index is covered in the [PHP API](../reference/php-api.md).

# What triggers a job

Before you change a job, walk back from it to every event and route that leads to it.

```php
use Lucasp\Loom\Index\IndexLoader;

$index = (new IndexLoader)->fromFile('storage/loom/index.json');

// Walks back from a dispatching method to the events and routes that reach it.
$callers = function (string $method, string $indent = '', array $path = []) use (&$callers, $index): void {
    foreach ($index->routes() as $route) {
        if ("{$route->controllerFqcn}::{$route->controllerMethod}" === $method) {
            echo "{$indent}route {$route->method} {$route->uri}\n";
        }
    }

    $listener = $index->findListener(strstr($method, '::', true) ?: $method);
    foreach ($listener?->handles ?? [] as $handle) {
        echo "{$indent}handles {$handle->event}\n";
        foreach (in_array($handle->event, $path, true) ? [] : $index->dispatchersOf($handle->event) as $site) {
            echo "{$indent}  dispatched from {$site->method}\n";
            $callers($site->method, "{$indent}    ", [...$path, $handle->event]);
        }
    }
};

foreach ($index->findJob('App\Jobs\SendMail')?->dispatchedFrom ?? [] as $site) {
    echo "dispatched from {$site->method}\n";
    $callers($site->method, '  ');
}
```

```text title="Output"
dispatched from App\Listeners\SendReceipt::handle
  handles App\Events\OrderPlaced
    dispatched from App\Http\Controllers\OrderController::store
      route POST /orders
```

Each step reads one link: the job's `dispatched_from`, the listener's `handles`, the event's `dispatched_from`, and the route whose controller method matches. The `impact-of-change` [MCP tool](../reference/mcp-tools.md) looks the other way: what a class handles, and which events would lose their last handler.

# Routes without auth

List every route whose middleware has no `auth` entry.

```php
use Lucasp\Loom\Index\IndexLoader;

$index = (new IndexLoader)->fromFile('storage/loom/index.json');

foreach ($index->routes() as $route) {
    $guarded = collect($route->middleware)->contains(fn (string $name): bool => str_starts_with($name, 'auth'));

    if (! $guarded) {
        echo "{$route->method} {$route->uri}  {$route->file}:{$route->line}\n";
    }
}
```

```text title="Output"
GET /health  routes/web.php:8
```

Middleware names are recorded as written, with groups such as `web` not expanded ([`routes[]`](../reference/schema.md#routes)), so a group that adds `auth` elsewhere is not seen here.

# Fail on new unresolved dispatches

Accept the dispatches Loom can't resolve today and fail the build on any new one.

```bash
# Once, from a scan of your main branch:
mkdir -p .loom && cp storage/loom/index.json .loom/baseline.json

# On every branch:
php artisan loom:scan
php artisan loom:check --baseline=.loom/baseline.json --skip=orphan-listeners --skip=orphan-events --skip=cyclic-dispatch
```

```text
unresolved-dispatches — No new unresolved dispatches (strict: none at all)
  ✗ Unresolved dispatch (dynamic_class_name) at app/Services/Notifier.php:9: event($eventClass)
1 violation(s) across 1 rule(s).
```

Only the dispatch the branch added fails, and the command exits `1`. Entries match on file, line and expression, so moving old code makes it look new: refresh the baseline when you accept it. Drop the `--skip` options to run every [rule](../reference/check-rules-and-formats.md#rules); `--strict` fails on every unresolved dispatch.

# Commands

Loom adds five Artisan commands, which read or write one index, by default `storage/loom/index.json`.

```bash
php artisan loom:scan                    # scan the app and write the index
php artisan loom:show OrderPlaced        # print the index, filtered
php artisan loom:diff old.json new.json  # compare two indexes
php artisan loom:check                   # run the policy rules
php artisan loom:mcp                     # serve the index over MCP
```

## loom:scan

```bash
php artisan loom:scan [--output=PATH] [--path=DIR ...] [--route-path=DIR ...] [--allow-empty] [-v]
```

Parses the app without booting it, validates the result against the [schema](schema.md) and writes the index. The directories come from [scan configuration](scan-config.md).

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--output=` | Write the index here instead of the configured `index_path`. A relative path resolves from the project root. The MCP server and UI keep reading `index_path`. |
| `--path=` | Scan this directory instead of `scan.paths`. Relative to the project root; glob patterns allowed. Repeatable. |
| `--route-path=` | Read routes from this directory instead of `scan.route_paths`. Same rules as `--path`. Repeatable. |
| `--no-discover-routes` | Do not follow route-file loading calls for this run, as if `scan.discover_routes` were false. Wins over the config value. |
| `--allow-empty` | Write an index even when the scan directories hold no PHP files, instead of failing. |

It prints the path written, the files read and a count per section. `-v` also lists each skipped file with its parser message and each route-file path not followed, with its reason:

```text
Loom index written to /var/www/shop/storage/loom/index.json
Scanned 16 PHP files in 1 directories.
events: 5, listeners: 6, observers: 0, model events: 0, jobs: 1, unresolved dispatches: 2, closure listeners: 1, scheduled tasks: 0, mailables: 0, notifications: 0, routes: 2, unresolved routes: 0, skipped files: 1
Skipped files:
  app/Broken.php:8  Syntax error, unexpected '}', expecting T_VARIABLE
```

A skipped file is skipped by every scanner and doesn't change the exit code.

| Exit code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | Index written, with or without skipped files |
| `1` | A scan path is invalid, the scan directories hold no PHP files without `--allow-empty`, the index failed schema validation, or the output could not be written. Nothing is written. |

## loom:show

```bash
php artisan loom:show [filter]
```

Prints the index as pretty JSON.

| Argument | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `filter` | Optional substring (a class or method name); keeps only events, listeners, observers and `model_events` entries whose JSON text contains it. |

The filter matches each entry's JSON text in events, listeners, observers and model events; other sections print in full. A filter with `/` or `\` never matches, because the JSON escapes them.

Exit `0` when printed, `1` when the index is missing, unreadable or not valid JSON.

## loom:diff

```bash
php artisan loom:diff old.json new.json --format=markdown
```

Compares two indexes by entry: added, removed and changed, not a text diff.

| Argument or option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `old` | Path to the old `index.json`. |
| `new` | Path to the new `index.json`. |
| `--format=` | Output format: text (default), json or markdown. |

Exit codes and output formats are in [Check rules and formats](check-rules-and-formats.md#exit-codes).

## loom:check

```bash
php artisan loom:check [index] --strict --baseline=main-index.json
```

Runs the policy rules against an index and fails when one is violated.

| Argument or option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `index` | Path to the index to check (default: `storage/loom/index.json`). |
| `--baseline=` | Path to an older `index.json`, for growth checks. |
| `--strict` | Treat any unresolved dispatch as a failure. |
| `--skip=` | Rule key to skip. Repeatable. |
| `--format=` | Output format: text (default), json or markdown. |

Rules, exit codes and formats are in [Check rules and formats](check-rules-and-formats.md).

## loom:mcp

```bash
php artisan loom:mcp
```

Starts a read-only [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server over stdio that serves the index and reloads it when the file changes. [MCP tools](mcp-tools.md) lists what it answers.

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--snapshot=` | Serve this index file instead of the default (`storage/loom/index.json`); it is never auto-scanned. |
| `--scan` | Run `loom:scan` before serving; cannot be combined with `--snapshot`. |
| `--no-scan` | Never auto-scan; the snapshot must already exist. |
| `--allow-empty` | Pass `--allow-empty` to `loom:scan` when this command scans. |

Exit `0` when the server stops normally, `1` when `laravel/mcp` isn't installed, `mcp.enabled` is `false`, the scan before serving fails or the server isn't registered.

Every config key is in [Index, UI and MCP configuration](ui-config.md) and [Scan configuration](scan-config.md).

# Check rules and output formats

The rules, exit codes and output formats of `loom:check` and `loom:diff`; the walkthrough is [Gate your CI](../guides/gate-your-ci.md).

```bash
php artisan loom:check storage/loom/index.json --baseline=.loom/baseline.json --format=json
php artisan loom:diff .loom/baseline.json storage/loom/index.json --format=markdown
```

Both read finished index files and need no source tree. Arguments and options are in [Commands](commands.md#loomcheck); in `loom:diff`, entries only in `new` are added and entries only in `old` are removed.

## Rules

| Key | Fails when | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `schema` | The index doesn't validate against the Loom schema. | Re-run `loom:scan`. |
| `orphan-listeners` | A listener handles no events. | Type-hint the event on `handle()`, register the listener, or delete it. |
| `orphan-events` | An event is never dispatched and never handled. | Delete it, or add the dispatch or listener that was meant to exist. |
| `unresolved-dispatches` | See below. | Make the dispatched class a literal class name, or accept it into the baseline. |
| `cyclic-dispatch` | A chain of dispatches loops back to its start. | Break one link in the reported chain. |

### Unresolved dispatches, baseline and strict

| Flags | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| Neither `--baseline` nor `--strict` | Passes without checking anything. |
| `--baseline=PATH` | Fails on any unresolved dispatch not in the baseline. |
| `--strict` | Fails on every unresolved dispatch, whatever the baseline says. |

Baseline entries match by file, line and expression, so moved code looks new; see the [recipe](../recipes/new-unresolved-dispatches.md).

### Cycle detection

`cyclic-dispatch` draws an edge from each event or job to what its handlers dispatch, and reports one representative cycle per back-edge: fix it, re-run, and the next one surfaces.

## Exit codes

| Command | Code | Meaning | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| check | `0` | Every rule that ran passed. | Nothing. |
| check | `1` | A rule found a violation. | Fix it or change the policy. Fail the job. |
| check | `2` | Nothing was checked: bad path, invalid JSON, unknown `--format`, unknown `--skip` key. | Fix the invocation. Fail the job too. |
| diff | `0` | No semantic changes. | Nothing. |
| diff | `1` | Changes exist. Not an error. | Post the diff. Fail only if you want drift to block. |
| diff | `2` | A path isn't a file, the JSON is invalid, or `--format` is unknown. | Fix the invocation. |

## Check output

### text

Rules with violations, then a count; a passing run prints `All checks passed.` With `--baseline`:

```text
orphan-listeners — Every listener handles at least one event
  ✗ Listener App\Listeners\AuditOrders handles no events.
orphan-events — Every event is dispatched or handled
  ✗ Event App\Events\OrderCancelled is never dispatched and never handled.
unresolved-dispatches — No new unresolved dispatches (strict: none at all)
  ✗ Unresolved dispatch (dynamic_class_name) at app/Services/Notifier.php:9: event($eventClass)
cyclic-dispatch — No cyclic event/job dispatch chains
  ✗ Cyclic dispatch: App\Events\InventoryAdjusted → App\Events\OrderPlaced → App\Events\InventoryAdjusted
4 violation(s) across 4 rule(s).
```

### json

Every rule appears, skipped ones included, so a consumer can tell what was enforced. The same run:


With `--skip=orphan-events` that rule reports as skipped:

```json

    "skipped": true,

```

### markdown

One section per failing rule, ready for a PR comment:

```markdown
## loom:check

### orphan-listeners — Every listener handles at least one event
- Listener App\Listeners\AuditOrders handles no events.

### orphan-events — Every event is dispatched or handled
- Event App\Events\OrderCancelled is never dispatched and never handled.

### unresolved-dispatches — No new unresolved dispatches (strict: none at all)

### cyclic-dispatch — No cyclic event/job dispatch chains
- Cyclic dispatch: App\Events\InventoryAdjusted → App\Events\OrderPlaced → App\Events\InventoryAdjusted
```

## Diff output

Sorted, so the same pair of indexes always gives the same output. No changes prints `No semantic changes.`, or `{}` as JSON.

`+` added, `-` removed, `~` changed with its changed members below. From a branch that added an event, two listeners and an unresolved dispatch:
